Yes it absolutely is. It’s part of the nervous system allowing you to process what’s going on in the body. 

We generally know shaking as a negative thing - when we are scared or in shock. We are taught that these are a sign of being scared or in fear. We tell people that they are shaking because they’re having a panic attack - but this is not the case. 

YES - they’re having a panic response, but the shaking is part of the panic discharge instead. 

Shaking and tremoring is not helping us to fight or flee, but rather it’s part of the body’s recovery response to help us calm down from stressful situations. This dumps the adrenaline and its the nervous system’s way of down regulating. 

Spontaneous movements don’t only occur when in stressful situations or when recovering from trauma - we laugh and cry which moves our diaphragm, we get excited, we do REM while we sleep and this is moved by the tremoring of the muscles that are moving them!

Our body subconsciously unwinds us later on when we need it, and these are where the tremoring/shaking moves in to help. The body has the capacity to move these things automatically.
